newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil says size of Varg field uncertain.
newsitem.headline: Statoil says size of Varg field uncertain.

text.p: Norway's Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Thursday that reserve estimates for Varg near the Sleipner area of the North Sea were still uncertain after the completion of an appraisal well.

Operator Saga Petroleum ASA recently completed the appraisal well on the field's northern flank, but no final conclusion can be drawn on the extent of the Varg reservoir until a sidetrack is completed, Statoil's company newsletter Status Weekly said.

"Saga is due to re-enter the same 15/12-10s well in the third quarter of 1997 to drill a sidetrack in a different direction to the present borehole," Statoil resource development official Svein Nedland told Status Weekly.
The discovery is currently thought to contain some 60 million barrels of oil, but the complexity of the reservoir makes this estimate uncertain, Statoil said.
A Varg development based on a production ship tied to a wellhead platform was approved by the government in May.
Saga has a 35 percent holding in the license and Statoil has another 35 percent. The government's direct financial interest makes up the remaining 30 percent.
